findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a Certified FOOD Protection Manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

On inspector arrival there was not a CFPM available at the facility. Staff at the time of the inspection indicated that the manager on duty had gone to another location to open there and would be back shortly. Mr. Annerino arrived during the inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts in an emergency.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12. 

An employee was observed to wash their hands and then use their bare hands to turn off the faucet, thus recontaminating their hands. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to review hand washing procedures with staff and monitor hand washing as needed to ensure that all hand washing procedures are conducted safely at all times moving forward.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x3) 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) Two of the slicers under the counter in the back prep area were observed with food debris remaining on them. They appeared to have been stored without proper cleaning. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean the food contact items within four hours of use. 2) (REPEAT x3) Soda nozzles in the drive thru area customer service area were observed soiled. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean them. The food contact surfaces were cleaned during this inspection to correct the immediate situation. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. 

There was an observed gap allowing light to enter through the bottom of the back door into the facility. This is an obvious possible pest entrance and should be repaired/resealed prior to the next routine inspection to prevent these possible pests. Ensure that all outer openings are sealed at all times.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Several fruit/drain flies were observed in the facility during the inspection. At the time of the inspection a large amount of the flies were observed in the dry storage room specifically around the mops and dump sink. The violation is NOT considered corrected at the time of the inspection and the PIC is instructed to continue working with their pest control agency for remedial action. The follow-up is being scheduled for one month to allow for remedial action to take effect.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display.

Raw eggs were observed stored over ready to eat foods on wire shelves in the walk in cooler. The PIC was shown and the eggs moved to correct. Ensure that all foods are stored according to their cooking temperatures in the facility at all times.

findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The soda nozzles in the drive thru area are observed soiled. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean them. findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Several fruit/drain flies were observed in the facility during the inspection. findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.110 Using Dressing Rooms and Lockers. (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. 

1) A monster energy drink was observed in the standing cooler next to the prep line alongside foods intended for consumers. 2) (REPEAT) A phone was observed on the table in the back next to equipment and with food nearby. The situations were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that all employee personal items are stored so that they do not pose a concern for contamination of consumer foods. Ensure that all personal items are stored away from food contact and preparation areas to prevent possible contamination of foods.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a Certified FOOD Protection Manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

The CFPM at the beginning of the inspection needed to leave without a replacement CFPM available to cover the shift. They stated that the night manager was in the process of trying for the certification but had not yet attained it. Ensure that there is always at least 1 CFPM present during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and:(H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

1) Employees are observed to don gloves without washing hands. 2) An employee was observed to adjust their pants and then don gloves and handle food without hand washing. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that when to conduct hand washing is reviewed with staff and enforced in the facility. Ensure hand washing is taking place prior to donning gloves and at any time that hands may have become contaminated prior to food handling.

4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

A crate in the walk in cooler used to store a sauce container off of the floor is observed with major white mold growth on it. The PIC was shown and removed the item for cleaning. Ensure that all non-food contact surfaces are maintained clean in the facility at all times.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

Make every effort to train and practice proper hand washing and single use glove use.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily.

Observed two wet wiping cloths to be out of sanitizer upon arrival. One was observed handing on the handle of a wire cart and the other was on the counter near the hand sink in front, behind the counter. Throughout the inspection the cloths were moved into sanitizer. Maintain wet wiping cloths in sanitizer when not actively being used. The violation is considered to be corrected on site.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Observed floors to be soiled. Floors in kitchen around drain pipe and under equipment have areas that are difficult to clean. Take care to sweep and then mop to remove dirt and debris from the floor. Floors in the storage areas along the walls have some accumulated soil. Also floors in the prep kitchen area have glue boards that needed to be removed. They were removed immediately. 
The hood vent is also starting to have some dust accumulation. The company (CFS) is are scheduled to provide maintenance within two weeks.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed the ceiling of the kitchen near the vent above the nacho cheese dispenser to have dust accumulation. Ensure routine cleaning of non-food contact surfaces. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 9/20/21 and 1/26/22.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed the following places to have an accumulation of debris, dust, and/or food splash:
1. Baffles of the hood have an accumulation of debris. Discussed increasing the professional hood cleaning occurrences. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 5/27/21 and 9/20/21.
2. Shelving and plastic covers at the nacho cheese dispenser shelving in the kitchen have accumulation of food debris and dust. The lower shelving of the fryer cart near the fry station has an accumulation of dust. This is a repeat violation since the last inspection on 9/20/21.
3. Ceiling of kitchen near the vent above the nacho cheese dispenser has accumulation of dust. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 9/20/21.
4. The warmer above the prep table has an accumulation of dust above it (on the hanging device as well attached to the ceiling).

Ensure routine cleaning of nonfood-contact surfaces. Discussed with PIC.

6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the new kitchen hand sink to lack caulking between the sink and wall. Caulk before the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:

3. Shelves of the walk-in cooler have food splash and debris - wash, rinse, sanitize.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed both sani buckets to be 0 ppm. PIC changed the quat in the buckets upon request - 400 ppm. COS. Ensure routine changing of sanitizer in buckets to maintain 200 to 400 ppm of quat at all times.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:

Observed no test strips for the lactic acid spray bottle sanitizer. Discussed with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 9/30/21.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12  (P) Food employee improperly washed hands. Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. Reference 2-301.12.

Observed multiple employees to wash hands improperly. A barrier must be used to turn off hand sink. Employee's turned off hand sink with clean hands, then dried with paper towels. Discussed proper hand washing technique with PIC. Each hand sink has a appropriate hand washing technique sign above it. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114  (P) Quaternary ammonium sanitizer measured 0 ppm at disposible sani towel dispenser. Maintain concentration at 200 ppm to 400 ppm as indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114.

Facility has been trying a disposible towel dispenser with quat added to the product. Inspector registered 0 ppm upon trying the solution. PIC added quat from 3 compartment sink. Product was then 200 ppm. COS.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Fans of walk-in cooler and walk-in freezer (food contact surface) are soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

Observed fans of walk-in cooler and walk-in freezer soiled with dust and debris. Food contact surfaces must be routinely washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Inspector will follow-up on 7/8/20.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on thawed corn dogs, cooked beans, and opened chiptole sauce. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

Observed several food items within walk-in cooler to lack appropriate date marking: thawed corn dogs, beans within large storage container (cooled with ice wands), and opened chiptole sauce. Discussed routine date marking with PIC. Facility typically date marks appropriately. COS.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.citation_text:
3-302.12  (C) Food storage containers are not labeled. Identify food storage containers with common name of the food. Reference 3-302.12.

Observed facility to have food storage containers that are not labeled: sugar and cinnamon sugar. Discussed labeling containers with common names of foods. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/2/20.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

Observed multiple in-use rags to be on counter and not within sanitization solution. Discussed need for rags to be within sanitization solution at all times. If utilizing spray bottle of sanitization (quat or bleach), clean paper towels should be utilized and disposed of after each use. COS.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-101.19  (C) Nonfood-contact surfaces of walk-in freezer is no longer easily cleanable. Reference 4-101.19.

Observed walk-in freezer to have an accumulation of frost at fan that is dripping and pooling into large areas of ice onto the ground. Discussed routine cleaning of walk-in freezer to hinder frost accumulation. Suggested servicing walk-in freezer. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/2/20.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15  (C) The plumbing needs repair. Repair according to Illinois and local plumbing code.  Reference 5-205.15.

Observed prep line hand sink to have a constant drip. Ensure hand sink is repaired according to Illinois and local plumbing code. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/2/20.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-201.11  (C) Caulking throughout was found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

Observed caulking throughout the facility to be in a state of disrepair and need re-done. Areas included prep line hand sink, 3 compartment sink, utility prep sink in back. Discussed repairs with PIC.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use.
(B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 
(C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. Reference 5-205.11.

Observed chicken debris in the hand sink. Discussed that hand sinks are for hand washing only and dumping of food and/or liquids should not occur in hand sink. Cease practice. COS.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14  (P) Employee changed gloves without washing hands between tasks. Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Reference 2-301.14.

Observed employee to assist inspector with understanding the scoops within bulk items by donning gloves, then retrieving ground beef to cook at back cook line. Employee did not wash hands before donning gloves. Discussed need to wash hands before donning gloves and changing tasks. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Grated shelving units (food contact surfaces) are soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

Observed multiple grated shelving units (food contact surfaces) soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Areas included: walk-in cooler (above ground beef), dry storage area, and reach-in cooler by prep line. Discussed routine cleaning of food contact surfaces with PIC. Inspector will follow-up with status of shelving units on 3/11/20.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.citation_text:
3-302.12  (C) Food storage containers are not labeled. Identify food storage containers with common name of the food. Reference 3-302.12.

Observed multiple areas where food storage containers are not labeled. Items included sugar, cinnamon sugar, salt, and dehydrated onions. Discussed labeling containers with common names of foods.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-901.11  (C) Equipment/Utensils are not properly Air-Dried after cleaning and sanitizing at dish drying rack. After cleaning and sanitizing all equipment and utensils shall be air dried before use. Reference 4-901.11.

Observed multiple stacks of equipment to be stacked and not air drying properly after being washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Items were on the top drying rack by the 3 compartment sink. Discussed with PIC that all equipment and utensils should be properly air-dried before being stacked.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-101.19  (C) Nonfood-contact surfaces of walk-in freezer is no longer easily cleanable. Reference 4-101.19.

Observed walk-in freezer to have an accumulation of frost at fan. Discussed routine cleaning of walk-in freezer to hinder accumulation of frost.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15  (C) The plumbing needs repair. Repair prep line hand sink according to Illinois and local plumbing code.  Reference 5-205.15.

Observed prep line hand sink to have a constant drip. Ensure hand sink is repaired according to Illinois and local plumbing code.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

Observed sani bucket with wet in-use wiping cloths; however, no sanitization solution was present in bucket. In-use wiping cloths must be contained within proper sanitizer solution. This is a repeat violation for the 2019 inspection year.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15 - Employee was observed making a nacho order with gloves, then moving to a new task of stirring cooking ground beef, placing hands in pockets, then returning to stirring ground beef. Employee was advised on proper glove use. 

Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation. This is a repeat violation for the 2019 inspection year.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Lettuce measured at 46F-47F in numerous containers stacked 2 high located in the 2 door upright cooler. PIC indicated lettuce was cut prior to lunch. PIC indicated the cooler was opened often for lunch time rush. Discussed prepping less lettuce at once to limit time for temperature increase. Discussed allowing lettuce to cool prior to placing in upright coolers. 

-> Cold holding items must be maintained below 41F. Please monitor temperatures to ensure they are maintained below 41F. When cold holding temperatures rise above 41F, items must be actively cooled. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
2 cans of domestic raid flying bug killer found stored on metal shelf in the back dry storage room with chemical storage and single use utensil storage. Cans removed by PIC during inspection. 

->Domestic residential pesticides are not approved for storage or use in a retail food establishment. Reference 7-206.11.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Unshielded glass lightbulbs noted in dry storage room above dry food items.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12  & 2-301.14 Employee in back prep did not wash hands between glove changes. Employee was advised on handwashing and was then observed washing hands without proper technique. Employee shut off the manual faucet prior to retrieving paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed with employee. 

Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must be washed any time they may have been contaminated and before putting on gloves/between glove changes. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 & 4-602.11 Dicer in the prep area used for white onions and tomatoes had food debris stuck on the slicing surface. Manager stated it was last used the day prior. Dicer was taken to dish area to go through ware washing process again.  
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses. 

Quesadilla slicer in-use since start of service was observed soiled with food debris. Slicer was taken to dish area to go through ware washing. 
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils used with time/temperature control for safety food shall be cleaned and sanitized throughout the day at least every 4 hours. Properly clean and sanitize in-use food contact equipment and utensil between uses and up to every 4hrs after continuous use.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Damp wiping cloth was observed on the counter next to the quesadilla press. Employee noted it was used to wipe down the make line after wetting it with sanitizer at the 3 part sink chemical dispenser. Sani-bucket was emptied since lunch service and not yet replaced. Store manager prepared the sani-bucket (200ppm quat) and placed wiping cloths in the solution to allow for proper storage between uses. 

Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15 - Employee was observed touching general surfaces of equipment (handle of walkin cooler door and handle of reach-in freezer) and not changing gloves prior to retrieving food from the reach-in freezer. Employee was advised on proper glove use and was later observed changing gloves between tasks
NOTE: General surfaces, such as the handles of equipment, are not considered clean surfaces, and gloves need to be changed after touching such surfaces. Educational handout was provided on proper glove use. 

Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation
